hypothesis: A causally observed burst of forced BTC short-liquidation buying may contain incremental information about near-term bullish continuation after conditioning on post-burst price and book persistence, but an exhaustion reversal is an equally plausible competing mechanism and no directional edge is currently established.
decision: Retain only as a source-qualification candidate. The frozen post-frontier public-recorder prefix has exact raw-Parquet-to-DuckDB parity and can supply gap-excluding public book, trade, and asset-context covariates, but one declared 2.307-second multi-channel disconnect occurred and the public trade schema has no liquidation flag. The public recorder therefore cannot supply the causal forced-liquidation treatment label or replace the still-unacquired official node-fill sample. Do not inspect strategy outcomes, specify entry thresholds, request requester-pays data, or change V58 under this revision.
falsifier: Invalidate the public-context qualification if a later immutable import changes any frozen-prefix row count or normalized row-stream SHA-256, reveals undeclared gaps, or proves source-timestamp semantics unsuitable for causal alignment. Invalidate the official-source requirement only if a separately verified non-billable source provides explicit liquidation metadata, causal event time, side semantics, and declared-window completeness. Update the strategy assessment only after an independently preregistered continuation-versus-exhaustion test passes realistic after-cost validation.
